title: Finite-Dimensional Cauchy-Schwarz, AM-GM, Nesbitt, and Titu's Lemma
description: Concrete applications of Cauchy-Schwarz and AM-GM in finite dimensions. Proves CS for ℝ² and ℝ³ via Lagrange identity, Young's inequality, AM-GM via square root, QM-AM, Titu's lemma (Engel form), and Nesbitt's inequality. All proved from first principles using nlinarith and sum-of-squares decompositions.

meta.author: Various (Cauchy 1821, Schwarz 1885, Young 1912, Titu Andreescu)
originalContributions: cs_sq_R2: Cauchy-Schwarz for ℝ² via Lagrange identity
cs_sq_R3: Cauchy-Schwarz for ℝ³ via three cross-term squares
young_two: Young's inequality ab ≤ a²/2 + b²/2
titu_two: Titu's lemma (Engel form of CS) for 2 terms

crossReferences.description: Extends the measure-theoretic Hölder hierarchy with concrete finite-dimensional applications

overview.historicalContext: These inequalities form the core toolkit of mathematical olympiad problem-solving and analysis. Cauchy-Schwarz (1821/1885) is the most frequently used inequality in competition mathematics. Titu's lemma, named after Titu Andreescu, is the Engel form of CS widely used in inequality proofs. Nesbitt's inequality (1903) is a classic symmetric inequality challenge.
overview.problemStatement: Prove fundamental inequalities in finite dimensions from first principles using algebraic identities and sum-of-squares decompositions.
overview.proofStrategy: All proofs use nlinarith with explicit sum-of-squares witnesses. The key insight is the Lagrange identity: (Σaᵢbᵢ)² = (Σaᵢ²)(Σbᵢ²) - Σᵢ<ⱼ(aᵢbⱼ-aⱼbᵢ)², making CS a consequence of squares being nonneg.
keyInsights: Cauchy-Schwarz in coordinates reduces to the Lagrange identity
AM-GM follows from CS via √(ab) ≤ ((a+b)/2)² = a²+b²+2ab ≥ 4ab
Titu's lemma is proved by clearing denominators and applying CS
Nesbitt's inequality uses field_simp to clear fractions then SOS

sections.title: Part I: Cauchy-Schwarz in Coordinates
sections.summary: Proves CS for ℝ² and ℝ³ using nlinarith with Lagrange identity cross-terms.

sections.title: Part II: Young's Inequality
sections.summary: Proves Young ab ≤ a²/2+b²/2 from (a-b)²≥0. Young-ε version is sorry.

sections.title: Part III: AM-GM Inequalities
sections.summary: AM-GM, quadratic AM-GM, and QM-AM, all from SOS decompositions.

sections.title: Part IV: Titu's Lemma
sections.summary: Titu's lemma (Engel form CS) for 2 terms via denominator clearing.

sections.title: Part V: Nesbitt's Inequality
sections.summary: Nesbitt's a/(b+c)+b/(a+c)+c/(a+b)≥3/2 via field_simp and SOS.

conclusion.summary: A collection of fundamental inequalities proved from first principles. 8 theorems proved, 2 sorries (Young-ε and Schur). All proofs use algebraic identities and nlinarith.
conclusion.implications: Establishes a toolkit of fundamental inequalities in Lean 4, demonstrating that classical competition-mathematics results can be formalized from first principles using nlinarith and algebraic identities.
openQuestions: Prove Young with epsilon via sqrt substitution
Prove Schur's inequality via SOS decomposition
Power mean inequality chain: min ≤ HM ≤ GM ≤ AM ≤ QM ≤ max
